title: Region gate: weighted p50/p95 latency and link-integrity scoring with tiered model fallbacks
creator: Aisha Rodriguez
description: Background: We need a deterministic gate that chooses POP/region and model variant by combining latency telemetry (p50 and p95) with a link-integrity network score. Current region selection uses separate heuristics for latency percentiles and simple link thresholds which produce oscillation during transient network noise and causes higher-than-expected tail latency and more fallbacks for tiered customers. This ticket defines and implements a composite region-gate that: 1) consumes continuous p50/p95 latency windows (15s and 5m EWMA), 2) ingests network health signals (packet-loss, TCP retransmit rate, recent connection errors) to produce a 0-100 link-integrity score, 3) computes a normalized composite rank per POP that is stable to short blips but responsive to sustained degradation, and 4) applies tier-aware routing rules with explicit model-variant fallback policies.
updates: 2026-03-01 — Created ticket and attached spike notes: ran traceroutes and p50/p95 samplings across 8 POPs. Spike indicated high variance in p95 when packet-loss > 0.3%.

2026-03-04 — Design review with PM and Observability: agreed to use weighted quantile fusion: score = w1 * normalized(p50) + w2 * normalized(p95) + w3 * (100 - link_integrity), initial weights 0.2 / 0.6 / 0.2. Added EWMA smoothing (alpha=0.2) for p95 to reduce oscillation.

2026-03-06 — Engineering spike: implemented proof-of-concept region-gate in sandbox. Exposed metrics: region_gate.composite_score, region_gate.p50_ewma, region_gate.p95_ewma, region_gate.link_integrity. Verified with synthetic load; composite score correlated with manual ranking in 92% of windows.

2026-03-08 — Feedback from Reliability: lower weight on p95 produces fewer unnecessary cross-pop fallbacks but may hide growing tail trends. Decided to keep p95 weight dominant but add hysteresis and a cooldown window of 60s before switching region for an individual customer session.

2026-03-10 — Added tier routing rules: Premium customers can prefer local POP if composite_score <= 25, otherwise prefer same-region fallback POP; Best-effort customers will route to lowest-cost POP within the same region unless composite_score > 40 then route to cross-region low-latency POP. Documented model-variant fallback policy: on degraded POP composite_score > 50 fallback chain = (primary -> quantized-x8 variant with smaller KV cache -> short-context variant with context length cap) with token-budget-aware selection.

2026-03-12 — Open PR#2489 created for orchestration changes and feature flag region_gate_v2. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/2489. Added Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Region+Gate+v2+Design. Planning canary rollout to internal services next week.
Pending — Implement per-customer override controls, add dashboard panels for rollup counts of region switches, and finalize alert thresholds in PagerDuty policy 'RegionGate-Alerts'.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for composite scoring and smoothing logic included
Canary rollout to internal tenants shows <1% increase in region-switch churn compared to baseline and >=5% reduction in p95 tail latency for affected sessions
Dashboards show composite_score and link_integrity trending for every POP; alerts fire when composite_score > 60 for >5m in production
Documentation updated: Confluence design doc, API changelog for feature flag region_gate_v2, and runtime config schema documented in repo
PR merged and migration plan for existing region policies in runtime-1.22 release notes
